A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the material growth of strain-compensated 8 mu m quantum cascade lasers has been achieved.
strain-compensated QCLs can operate at room temperature with a low threshold current density.
the strain-compensated active region is an attractive candidate for mid-infrared lasers operating at room temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
strain compensation is an important factor for the realization of high-performance quantum cascade lasers at room temperature.
strain-compensated material can be grown at a high rate (similar to 1 mu m min(-1)) with a high uniformity (similar to 0.2% over 2 in wafer) and can lead to a high performance laser.
the strain-compensated active regions can be grown on the GaAs substrate without the need of a metamorphic buffer.
